_comment: Card ownership, granted by the controller. launch_gate reads launch_block_granted
and note; a false grant with no note reads as a stub, not as a decision.
Idle is not free: a card's owner is the job still running or the one the controller
has queued, never the instantaneous nvidia-smi row.
AND A STALE GRANT IS WORSE THAN NO GRANT (b0 2026-09-03): the 0-7 grant below outlived
the run it was made for, so the next launcher would have read it as licence to take
cards 4 and 7 -- which hold the USER'S OWN work in another container. The rule above
cuts both ways: a card's owner is not the nvidia-smi row, and it is not a superseded

cards.7: LANE, granted 05:52Z. Held the user's acc_spec_arms until ~05:45Z; that process is now on card 5, not gone. Currently b0's eval/score_matrix.py (host pid 4062191).

lane_note: Cards 6-7 are the lane, widened from 7 alone at 06:05Z because the lane had three queued jobs (b0's control row, de's all-to-all microbench, e1's pass@k) and a one-card lane that people must break is not a rule -- the same reasoning that put the one-job-at-a-time rule in AGENTS.md. The block stays 0-3 and NOTHING here licenses touching it. Cards 4 and 5 hold the USER'S OWN work in another container (grpo-gsm8k-27b; acc_spec_arms, which moved off card 7 between 05:45Z and 06:05Z) and are NEVER TAKE. Read nvidia-smi before claiming either lane card and yield to a user process rather than contending: the acc_spec move proves the user's container reassigns itself with no notice. Idle is not free -- this is a grant, not an inference from an nvidia-smi row.

superseded_2026_09_02.note: Granted for the 500M/20B run on ALL EIGHT cards, user ruling 2026-09-02. The lane is gone by that ruling and the cost was stated before it was taken: in-run milestone generation sweeps cannot run, because the scorer needs a whole 95 GiB card and not a gap -- observed, not derived, when the probe's scorer took card 7 alone after training exited. End-of-run scoring is unaffected: run_ddp.sh scores after torchrun exits, when all eight are free. Second cost: the 200M comparison axis loses its free pin at step 17,500 and needs 15,313 plus conversion. Both were on the table before the decision. Resume was PROVEN before this grant, per the user's order of 2026-09-02: six conditions, nine domains character-for-character, plus a reverse test that made the guard fire. --auto-resume is 1 and not more: the cursor is per-segment, so a second resume re-reads 10,240 rows and nothing has ever tested it.

lane_two_card_exception: GRANTED 2026-09-03, narrow, one job: de's dist.all_to_all_single microbench may hold BOTH lane cards at once. The 06:05Z widening was three jobs one card each and de read it correctly as not covering this. The exception is not 'big jobs may take two': it is that MEASURING A LINK REQUIRES TWO ENDPOINTS -- a two-rank all_to_all on one card is a device-to-device copy and measures nothing about NVLink, so there is no one-card version of this job to fall back to. Bounded by occupancy, not by importance: 110 MB x ~10 repeats is SECONDS. Any job that structurally needs two endpoints AND occupies seconds qualifies; a job that merely runs faster on two cards does not. ORDERING: card 6 is held IDLE until b0's score_matrix row on card 7 finishes, then de takes 6+7, then e1's pass@k starts on 6. Holding one card idle for the ~20 min of b0's row is the price of not queueing a seconds-long job behind an hours-long one -- a queue ordered by arrival makes the lane slower than no lane.
